facts.text: Adams Avenue sits in West Adams, one of Los Angeles’ oldest neighborhoods, with most homes built between 1880 and 1925.
The area boasts more than 70 sites that have earned recognition as Los Angeles Historic‑Cultural Monuments, California Historical Landmarks, or National Register listings.
West Adams houses the largest collection of historic houses west of the Mississippi, showcasing styles from Queen Anne to Mediterranean Revival.
The neighborhood’s historic buildings include the William Andrews Clark Memorial Library, a landmark that opened in 1915.
The Metro E Line serves West Adams with stops at Vermont/Expo and Expo/Western, linking the area to downtown and Santa Monica.
Adams Avenue runs through the historic districts of Kensington, Normal Heights, and University Heights, each known for their early 20th‑century architecture.
